0.12.0 is a score release. The score moves to model core-v7, which charges a decision once rather than every site that repeats it, and the reworded rule texts it ships with change the finding ids of five rules. The corpus was replayed once under the new model on 2026-11-16; every pinned subject keeps or raises its score, and none changes band except anyhow, which moves from Needs work to Great. See [Breaking changes](#breaking-changes).

## Breaking changes

### Scores move to model core-v7

**Before.** `audit.score.model` was `core-v6`.

**After.** `audit.score.model` is `core-v7` ([9aef6c7](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/9aef6c7)). `rust-doctor.com/share` links that carry `m=core-v6` now render as a number from a retired model.

Who is affected: anything that compares `audit.score.value` across versions, or pins the model string.

**Upgrade path.** Rescan with 0.12.0 before you compare a score against a new one. A score recorded under core-v6 is not comparable.

| Value | core-v6 record | core-v7 record |
|---|---|---|
| `SCORE_MODEL` | `core-v6` | `core-v7` |
| `complex_function` corpus noise | 8709 bp (27 of 31) | 6363 bp (7 of 11), still withheld |
| `oversized_unit` corpus noise | 3333 bp (13 of 39) | 2647 bp (9 of 34) |
| `duplicate_major_versions` agent-population noise | unmeasured | 7500 bp (6 of 8) |
| Median score, healthy population | 89.00 | 93.00 |
| Median score, agent population | 81.00 | 88.50 |

### Reworded messages change finding ids

A finding id hashes its rule, its location and its message, so each reworded message below gives its findings new ids ([7f6f4d9](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/7f6f4d9), [9aef6c7](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/9aef6c7), [9c11c8b](https://github.com/arthjean/rust-doctor/commit/9c11c8b)):

- `rust_doctor::structure::unreferenced_feature`: "which no cfg reads" becomes "which no cfg and no build script reads".
- `rust_doctor::cargo::permissive_lint_table`: the message gains ", which hides N findings in this package." The scope reads "in the packages that inherit it" for a workspace entry, and the count reads "no finding" or "1 finding" at those values. No count is printed when Clippy did not lint every member the entry covers, as under `--package` or when a member does not compile.
- `rust_doctor::structure::oversized_unit`: a file reads "is N lines long, M outside test code." instead of "is N lines long.".
- `rust_doctor::cargo::duplicate_major_versions`: "required by" names up to three members in name order, then "+N more"; "through" names the first non-member crate on a shortest path, ties broken by name; versions are listed in semver order. A duplicate a member can remove is now anchored at that member's `Cargo.toml` instead of `Cargo.lock`, which changes its id too, and every other duplicate publishes at `info`.
- `rust_doctor::repo::secret_in_build_step`: a variable the workspace embeds with `env!` or `option_env!` is reported at `info` with a new message naming the embedding site: "... embeds it in the binary: whatever it holds ships to every user."

Help texts and titles changed too, without changing any id: `clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks` offers a `// SAFETY:` comment or an `#[expect(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks, reason = "...")]`, `orphan_module_file` says "Declare the file with a mod declaration. Remove it only if nothing should compile it.", and `blocking_call_in_async` names your runtime's blocking pool (`spawn_blocking`, `unblock`) instead of one runtime. Findings on a `workspace = true` dependency now point at the member's own line for that key, with their id unchanged.

Who is affected: anything that stores finding ids across versions, such as a saved report or a dashboard keyed on `diagnostics[].id`. A `--scope baseline` run scans both sides with the same binary, so its pairing is unaffected.

**Upgrade path.** Regenerate stored reports with 0.12.0. A finding of the rules above recorded by an earlier release reads as fixed, and its new id as introduced.

## Corpus replay

The pinned corpus was replayed once under core-v7, on Linux with toolchain 1.99.1. One subject moved by more than 10 points:

| Subject | Population | core-v6 | core-v7 | Why |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| syncvibe | agent | 80 | 91 | Its three `duplicate_major_versions` warnings sit in `Cargo.lock`, where no member requirement can remove them, so they publish at `info` and Dependencies rises from 37 to 100. `complex_function` now requires both of its thresholds and is published at `info` as a distrusted rule, so its 16 sites fall to 10 and Maintainability rises from 69 to 79. |

Every other subject moved by 8 points or less, upward.

## Install

```bash
npx rust-doctor@latest
```

```bash
cargo install rust-doctor --locked
```

```bash
cargo binstall rust-doctor
```
